subject: Evaluation playbook & next steps — clarifying quality criteria
messages:

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo recap + quick clarifying questions

Hi Jane — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and a couple clarifying questions so we can prepare the evaluation artifacts you asked for: 

1) Goal we heard: replace a mix of in-house LLM endpoints and hyperscaler managed endpoints for internal SRE runbooks and incident classification. Key success metrics you mentioned: <10% hallucination rate on the incident-answer prompts, P95 latency < 300ms for short queries, and predictable token cost under our monthly projection.

2) Next deliverables from our side: an evaluation playbook (sample prompts + scoring rubric), a cost/latency comparison runbook vs. Bedrock/Vertex, and a short private deployment checklist if you want to test in VPC.

Clarifying Qs (super short):
- Can you share a rough monthly tokens per month number (or a range) so we size the bench?
- Are there particular prompt families to prioritize (e.g., root-cause synthesis, suggested remediation steps, playbook retrieval)?

I’m attaching a draft evaluation playbook and a sample prompt file — we’ll tailor them once you confirm the priority prompt families. Proposed next step: 30-min sync early next week to align on the acceptance criteria and testing windows.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>

Date: 2026-05-14T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + quick clarifying questions

Marissa — really helpful demo, thanks. A few answers and color: 

- Monthly tokens: currently 80M–120M tokens/month in the runbook/triage flows; early-stage but we expect growth as we onboard more teams.
- Priority prompts:
  * Incident synthesis (short): summarize the problem and likely root cause from structured logs + alert text.
  * Remediation suggestion: 2–3 actionable steps with confidence bands.
  * Playbook retrieval: given a short error string, return the canonical runbook link + one-sentence applicability note.

Competitors we’re benchmarking against: Bedrock (largest suite of base models we can call through their API) and Vertex AI endpoints (we have an internal baseline). Important buy signals for us: improved hallucination rates, deterministic behavior for repeat queries, and predictable latency under load. Also interested in private deployment options (VPC/on-prem) for the most sensitive teams.

Can you provide a proposed set of eval prompts and the scripts you’ll run so our infra team can give access where needed?

—Jane
Jane Doe
Sr. SRE, Acme Corp
jane.doe@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-15T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + quick clarifying questions

Thanks, Jane — this is perfect. Attaching the playbook & sample prompts we discussed and mapping the specific tests we recommend: 

Planned test matrix (high level):
- Quality: 1k prompts per family (synth, remediation, retrieval) -> automated throughput run, BLEU/ROUGE for retrieval, hallucination checks via oracle answers + human spot checks for synthesizers.
- Regression: run against your existing archived incidents (30-day window) to calculate hallucination rate and false-positive remediation suggestions.
- Performance: P95/P99 latency under a 50 RPS and 200 RPS staged load.
- Cost: tokenized cost model across Redwood-hosted variants + rough Bedrock/Vertex API cost projection for same prompt corpus.

Differentiators to highlight to the SRE team (summary):
- Unified runtime: same inference API + tooling whether you try hosted, dedicated, or VPC private — simplifies switching models and comparing performance.
- Prefix/KV caching: reduces cost for repeated retrieval queries (common in playbook retrieval).
- Rollout controls & fallbacks: can do canary by user group and automatic fallback to cheaper model variant if SLOs slip.
- Transparent per-token cost breakdowns in Console and token-level latency traces — helps root-cause perf regressions faster.

Attached files: acme-eval-playbook.xlsx (detailed rubric) and acme-sample-prompts.json (seed prompts + labeling guidance). A couple of practical asks for us to run the bench:
- A service account + short-lived API key we can use to push eval traffic (we’ll coordinate ephemeral keys).
- A sample of 200 archived incident texts we can run the regression checks against (de-identified).

Can we do a 30-min sync on Tuesday 05/19 at 11:00 AM PT to lock the acceptance criteria? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and loop in Sergio (bench lead) and Dylan (arch integration).

Best,
Marissa
